content: A text embedding is a list of numbers produced by a model. Texts with related meanings often have vectors that are close together in the embedding space.
The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model produces 384 numbers for each text. The vector column in PostgreSQL must have the same number of dimensions as the model output.
Cosine similarity compares the direction of two vectors. For normalized vectors, their dot product is cosine similarity. A higher similarity means the texts are more alike.
In pgvector, the <=> operator calculates cosine distance. Distance is one minus cosine similarity, so smaller cosine distance means a closer match.
pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds a vector data type and operators for comparing vectors. The CREATE EXTENSION vector command enables it in a database.
An exact nearest-neighbor query sorts every candidate by vector distance and returns the closest k rows. Exact search is a useful baseline before adding an approximate index.
An HNSW index can speed up approximate nearest-neighbor search. It trades some recall for speed and should be evaluated against exact search on representative queries.
Use the same embedding model for stored documents and search queries. If the model changes, regenerate the document embeddings so every vector remains in the same embedding space.
